title: Culturing Drosophila egg chambers and imaging border cell migration
protocol: Set up fly crosses.
Collect newly hatched females of the correct genotype daily and place them into fresh vials with yeast, ensuring an equal number of males for egg production.
Avoid overcrowding the vials.
Place collected flies in empty fly vials and heat shock for 10 minutes in a water bath at 37°C to generate partial clones.
Store heat shocked flies at 25°C and transfer them to fresh yeast daily until imaged, usually from 2 to 5 days after the heat shock.
Place 2 or 3 day old females on wet yeast 2 or 3 days prior to dissection for clonal analysis.
For full border cell clusters, either apply three consecutive 1-hour heat shocks every 12 hours during the second and third larval instars or leave flies for 4-5 days after adult heat shock.
Pipette 150 μl of 0.1 mg/ml Poly-D-Lysine into each well of a LabTek chamber.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 to 2 hours.
Remove poly-Lysine and store at -20°C if reused later.
Wash coated dishes 4 times with water.
Aspirate excess water from the washed dishes.
Prepare dissection and culture media fresh each day.
Take 15ml of Schneider’s medium and add 7.5 μl Insulin for dissection media.
Warm dissection media to room temperature prior to dissection.
To prepare culture media, mix 965 μl Dissection media with 25 μl FCS, 10 μl Trehalose solution, 1 μl diluted ADA, 1 μl Methoprene, and 0.5 μl Ecdysone.
Keep the prepared culture media at room temperature for several hours.
Immediately before imaging, take 200 μl of culture media and add approximately 0.6 μl FM4-64.
Pull out ovaries with fine dissecting forceps from 1 to 2 anesthetized females in about 500 μl of dissecting medium in a glass dissecting chamber.
Use carbon dioxide to anesthetize individual flies and minimize anesthesia time.
Transfer the ovaries into a new well with fresh dissecting medium.
Use fine dissection pins to open up the ovaries and detach strings of ovarioles from each other.
Select an ovariole that contains an appropriate staged egg chamber.
Dissect single egg chambers of appropriate stages out from the muscle sheath.
Remove older stage egg chambers from the chain using a scissoring action with two needles.
Place the blunter pin near the target egg chamber and quickly drag the tungsten needle past it on the other side to remove the muscle sheath.
Repeat the process to remove younger egg chambers in the chain, keeping the blunter needle closest to the target egg chamber.
Learn how to distinguish appropriate stages of egg chambers with a dissecting microscope.

Use markers such as the relative size of the oocyte compared to the whole egg chamber, whether the oocyte has started to uptake yolk and become more opaque, and whether nurse cells are transparent or opaque due to lipid droplet accumulation.
Place the dish on a black background for better visualization.
Illuminate the dish from above or the side for easier stage discrimination.
Transfer single dissected egg chambers into a new well with dissecting medium using a pipette with a 2 μl or 20 μl tip.
Wash the egg chambers once more with medium and select the 5-10 nicest ones of the correct stage.
Transfer selected egg chambers into a poly-D-lysine coated imaging chamber in a total volume of about 10 μl.
Let egg chambers adhere briefly for approximately 5-10 seconds.
Carefully add 200 μl of imaging medium supplemented with FM4-64 just before use.
Limit dissection time to 15 minutes.
Maintain egg chambers for up to 3 hours in imaging media before morphological defects appear.
Use transmission and FM4-64 channels to select healthy looking egg chambers for imaging.
Choose egg chambers where border cells have clearly delaminated or are already migrating.
Exclude egg chambers with nurse cells or follicle cells showing greatly increased FM 4-64 uptake compared to their neighbors.
Avoid egg chambers that take up FM4-64 very poorly, as they may be unhealthy.
Use DIC and FM4-64 channels to assess the healthiness of egg chambers.
Set up the microscope using a 40x oil objective with a motorized stage if available.
Choose 3 to 8 good looking egg chambers for imaging.
Mark the position of selected egg chambers using the stage tool.
Set the plane where border cells are as the middle point of your future z stack.
Begin imaging.
Image egg chambers every 2 minutes for 2,5 hours at appropriate laser intensity.
Check morphology of egg chambers post-imaging to control for phototoxicity.
Use Zeiss browser to review and project timelapses.
Assess size increase in egg chamber from movie.
Evaluate growth of oocyte during imaging.
Observe follicle cell layer retraction towards the oocyte.
Monitor movement of nurse cell nuclei in the movie.
Ensure tight adherence of nurse cell membranes.
Determine end of imaging when nurse cell nuclei stop moving.
Identify end of imaging when nurse cell membranes become highly detached.
Recognize end of imaging when nurse cells adopt a rounded shape.
